title: Dal Tadka
description: A comforting yellow toor dal simmered until creamy and finished with a fragrant tempering of ghee, cumin, garlic, dried red chillies, and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 3 cups for pressure cooking, plus extra as needed

steps: Rinse the toor dal under running water 3-4 times until the water becomes relatively clear. Soak for 10 minutes while preparing the vegetables.
Add drained dal, turmeric, 3 cups water, and half the salt to a pressure cooker. Cook over medium-high flame for 3-4 whistles, approximately 12-15 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft.
Allow pressure to release naturally. Open the cooker and whisk the dal until creamy, adding warm water if needed to achieve a pourable consistency.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadai over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds; sauté for 30 seconds until they crackle and become fragrant.
Add chopped onion, ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Sauté over medium flame for 4-5 minutes until the onions turn golden and the raw garlic aroma disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes, red chilli powder, and remaining salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 5-6 minutes until tomatoes turn mushy and ghee begins separating around the masala.
Pour the cooked dal into the masala, add asafoetida, and simmer over low flame for 5-7 minutes until the flavours combine and small bubbles appear.
Heat the remaining ghee separately, add dried red chillies and a pinch of cumin, and let them sizzle for 20-30 seconds. Pour over the dal, garnish with coriander and lemon juice, and serve hot.
tips: Whisking cooked dal gives it a naturally creamy texture without requiring cream.
Add the final ghee tempering immediately before serving for the strongest aroma.

title: Rajma Masala
description: Traditional Punjabi kidney beans cooked slowly in a rich onion-tomato masala with ginger, garlic, and warming spices.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 4 cups for pressure cooking, plus extra as needed

steps: Wash rajma thoroughly and soak in 4 cups water for 8-12 hours. Drain and rinse again until the soaking water is completely discarded.
Transfer rajma to a pressure cooker with 4 cups fresh water and half the salt. Cook over medium-high flame for 20-25 minutes, approximately 6-8 whistles, until beans are completely soft.
Heat oil and ghee in a heavy-bottomed kadai over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and sauté for 20 seconds until they crackle and release their aroma.
Add finely chopped onions and cook over medium flame for 7-9 minutes, stirring regularly until deep golden brown and caramelised.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Sauté over medium-low flame for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears and the mixture becomes fragrant.

Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and remaining salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 10-12 minutes until the masala thickens and oil separates at the edges.
Add cooked rajma with 2 cups of its cooking liquid. Mash approximately 2 tbsp beans against the pan, then simmer over low flame for 15-20 minutes until the gravy becomes thick and glossy.
Add garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, simmer for another 2 minutes, and garnish with coriander. Rest covered for 5 minutes before serving with steamed rice.
tips: Rajma must be thoroughly cooked until completely tender; never rely on partially cooked beans.
The final slow simmer is essential for a thick, restaurant-style gravy.

title: Aloo Gobi Matar
description: A classic everyday Punjabi dry sabzi featuring tender cauliflower, potatoes, and peas coated in a fragrant ginger-tomato masala.
steps: Soak cauliflower florets in warm salted water for 10 minutes, rinse thoroughly, and drain. Peel and cube potatoes into similarly sized pieces for even cooking.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai over medium-high flame for 2-3 minutes until its sharp raw aroma disappears. Reduce flame to medium before adding spices.
Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Let the cumin crackle for 20-30 seconds until fragrant, then add chopped onions and sauté for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add grated ginger and green chillies. Sauté over medium flame for 1 minute until aromatic, then add chopped tomatoes and cook for 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 2 minutes until the masala thickens and oil begins separating.
Add potatoes and cauliflower, tossing gently until coated. Cover and cook over low flame for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables become almost fork-tender.
Add green peas and cook uncovered over medium-low flame for 4-5 minutes until peas soften and excess moisture evaporates.
Finish with garam masala, amchur, and coriander. Toss gently, cover for 2 minutes over low flame, and serve with fresh rotis.
tips: Keep the kadai covered during cooking to retain moisture without adding excessive water.
Add amchur at the end to preserve its tangy flavour.

title: Bhindi Masala
description: A simple everyday okra sabzi with caramelised onions, tomatoes, and dry Indian spices, cooked until tender without becoming slimy.
steps: Wash okra thoroughly and dry each piece completely with a clean towel. Trim the ends and cut into 1-inch pieces, ensuring no water remains.
Heat 1.5 tbsp mustard oil in a wide kadai over medium-high flame. Add okra and sauté for 6-8 minutes until lightly browned and the sticky texture reduces.
Remove okra and set aside. Add remaining oil to the same kadai, heat over medium flame, and add cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add sliced onions and sauté over medium flame for 5-6 minutes until golden brown and slightly caramelised at the edges.
Add grated ginger and green chillies. Cook over medium-low flame for 1 minute until fragrant, then add chopped tomatoes and sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook over low flame for 2 minutes until the spices become aromatic and the masala thickens.
Return cooked okra to the kadai and mix gently. Cook uncovered over medium-low flame for 5-6 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the masala coats them evenly.
Sprinkle amchur and garam masala, toss gently, and cook for another minute. Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.
tips: Never cut or cook wet okra because surface moisture increases sliminess.
Use a wide kadai and avoid frequent stirring to keep the pieces intact.

title: Palak Paneer
description: Soft paneer cubes simmered in a vibrant spinach gravy flavoured with garlic, ginger, green chillies, and mild Indian spices.
steps: Wash spinach thoroughly and remove thick stems. Bring water to a boil over high flame, blanch spinach for 2 minutes until wilted, then transfer immediately into cold water.
Drain spinach completely and blend with green chillies into a smooth puree. Avoid adding excessive water so the gravy remains thick.
Heat ghee in a kadai over medium flame. Add cumin seeds and chopped garlic, sautéing for 30-40 seconds until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add chopped onion and ginger. Sauté over medium flame for 4-5 minutes until onions turn translucent and the raw ginger aroma disappears.
Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 4-5 minutes until tomatoes become mushy and ghee separates slightly.
Pour in spinach puree and simmer over low flame for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally until the gravy thickens and develops a rich green colour.
Add paneer cubes and garam masala. Simmer gently over low flame for 3-4 minutes until paneer absorbs the flavours without breaking.
Stir in cream and lemon juice, cook for another 30 seconds over low flame, and serve immediately with roti or jeera rice.
tips: Blanching spinach briefly and cooling it immediately helps preserve its green colour.
Avoid boiling the gravy vigorously after adding paneer, as the cubes can become rubbery.

title: Jeera Rice
description: Fluffy long-grain basmati rice gently cooked with ghee, toasted cumin seeds, and whole spices for a simple aromatic accompaniment.
steps: Wash basmati rice gently 3-4 times until the water runs mostly clear. Soak in fresh water for 20 minutes, then drain completely.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium flame. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom; sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add cumin seeds and cook over medium-low flame for 20-30 seconds until they crackle and release their nutty fragrance without turning dark.
Add drained rice and gently stir over medium-low flame for 1-2 minutes until every grain is coated with fragrant ghee.
Pour in water and add salt. Increase to medium-high flame and bring to a gentle boil for approximately 3-4 minutes until bubbles appear across the surface.
Reduce flame to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 10-12 minutes until the water is absorbed and rice grains become tender.
Turn off the flame and let the rice rest covered for 5 minutes. This allows residual steam to finish cooking the grains without making them mushy.
Fluff gently with a fork, remove whole spices if desired, garnish with coriander, and serve hot.
tips: Do not stir the rice repeatedly while cooking, as this can break the long grains.
The resting period after cooking is important for separate, fluffy grains.

title: Chana Masala
description: A hearty Punjabi chickpea curry cooked in a tangy onion-tomato gravy with roasted cumin, coriander, amchur, and aromatic garam masala.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 4 cups for pressure cooking, plus extra as needed

ingredients.name: black tea
ingredients.amount: 1 tsp, tied in a clean muslin pouch (optional)

steps: Wash chickpeas thoroughly and soak in plenty of water for 8-12 hours. Drain and rinse before cooking to remove the soaking liquid.
Add chickpeas, 4 cups fresh water, half the salt, and optional tea pouch to a pressure cooker. Cook over medium-high flame for 20-25 minutes, approximately 6-8 whistles, until completely tender.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium flame. Add cumin seeds and sauté for 20 seconds until they crackle and smell toasted.
Add chopped onions and cook over medium flame for 6-8 minutes, stirring regularly until golden brown and caramelised.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Sauté over medium-low flame for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears and the mixture becomes fragrant.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and remaining salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 8-10 minutes until tomatoes break down and oil separates.
Add cooked chickpeas with 1.5 cups cooking liquid. Mash a small portion of chickpeas against the kadai and simmer over low flame for 12-15 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Add amchur and garam masala, simmer for 2 minutes over low flame, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve with bhature, roti, or rice.
tips: Mashing a small portion of chickpeas naturally thickens the gravy without adding cream.
Remove the optional tea pouch after cooking; it provides a deeper brown colour without strongly changing the flavour.

title: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoky roasted brinjal mashed and cooked with onions, tomatoes, garlic, green chillies, and mustard oil for a rustic Punjabi favourite.
steps: Wash and dry the brinjal completely. Make 3-4 shallow slits and insert a few garlic pieces into the cuts for extra flavour.
Roast brinjal over a medium-high gas flame, turning every 2-3 minutes for approximately 12-15 minutes until the skin is charred and the flesh feels completely soft.
Place the roasted brinjal in a covered bowl for 5 minutes over no flame, allowing the steam to loosen the charred skin. Peel and mash the flesh, removing any burnt skin.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai over medium flame for 2 minutes until its sharp raw smell disappears. Add cumin seeds and sauté for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped onions and cook over medium flame for 5-6 minutes until golden. Add remaining garlic, ginger, and green chillies; sauté for 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 6-8 minutes until tomatoes become mushy and oil separates from the masala.
Add mashed roasted brinjal and mix thoroughly. Cook uncovered over medium-low flame for 6-8 minutes until the bharta thickens and develops a smoky, roasted aroma.
Finish with fresh coriander, mix gently, and cook for another minute over low flame. Serve hot with roti or paratha.
tips: Choose a large, heavy brinjal with smooth skin and relatively few seeds.
Roasting directly over a flame gives the traditional smoky flavour that oven roasting may not fully reproduce.

title: Matar Mushroom
description: A comforting everyday mushroom and green pea curry cooked in a lightly spiced tomato-onion gravy with ginger, garlic, and garam masala.
steps: Clean mushrooms using a damp cloth or quick rinse, pat completely dry, and quarter them. Shell fresh peas if using fresh vegetables.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium-high flame. Add mushrooms and sauté for 4-5 minutes until their moisture releases, evaporates, and the edges develop light golden spots.
Remove mushrooms and set aside. In the same kadai, add cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped onions and sauté over medium flame for 5-6 minutes until golden brown. Add ginger, garlic, and green chillies, cooking for another 1-2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt. Cook over medium-low flame for 7-8 minutes until the masala thickens and oil separates around the edges.
Add green peas and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook over medium-low flame for 5-7 minutes until peas become tender and the gravy develops a gentle simmer.
Return mushrooms to the kadai and mix gently. Cook uncovered over low flame for 4-5 minutes until the mushrooms absorb the masala and the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Add garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, optional cream, and fresh coriander. Simmer for another minute over low flame and serve hot with roti or rice.
tips: Sautéing mushrooms separately prevents excess released water from diluting the masala.
Add cream only after reducing the flame to maintain a smooth gravy.

title: Vegetable Pulao
description: A fragrant one-pot rice dish with basmati rice, seasonal vegetables, whole spices, and mild aromatics, ideal for everyday family meals.
steps: Wash basmati rice gently 3-4 times until the water runs mostly clear. Soak for 20 minutes, then drain completely to help the grains cook evenly.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium flame. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom; sauté for 30 seconds until the whole spices release their fragrance.
Add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle for 20 seconds. Add sliced onion and cook over medium flame for 4-5 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Sauté over medium-low flame for 1-2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears and the mixture becomes fragrant.
Add carrots, beans, potatoes, and peas. Stir-fry over medium flame for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables are lightly coated with ghee and begin softening.
Add turmeric, garam masala, salt, and drained rice. Toss gently over low flame for 1-2 minutes until the rice grains are coated without breaking.
Pour in measured water, increase to medium-high flame, and bring to a boil for approximately 3 minutes until bubbles appear across the surface.
Cover tightly, reduce flame to low, and cook for 10-12 minutes until the water is absorbed and vegetables are tender. Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff gently, garnish with coriander, and serve.
tips: Use equal-sized vegetable pieces so they cook evenly.
Avoid stirring repeatedly after adding water because it can break the rice grains and make the pulao sticky.

title: Aloo Paratha
description: Whole-wheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes, green chillies, coriander, and ajwain, cooked until golden and crisp with ghee.
steps: Combine the whole wheat flour, 1/2 tsp salt, and oil in a mixing bowl. Gradually add water and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes kneading until the dough feels pliable and no dry flour remains. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.

Mash the boiled potatoes thoroughly in a bowl until no large lumps remain. Add chopped green chillies, coriander, cumin powder, ajwain, red chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, and remaining salt. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 2-3 minutes until the filling is evenly seasoned and dry enough to handle.

Divide the dough and potato filling into 8 equal portions. Roll one dough portion into a small circle, place one portion of filling in the centre, and bring the edges together to seal it. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 2 minutes assembling each paratha until the filling is enclosed without gaps.

Dust the stuffed dough lightly with flour and roll gently into a paratha approximately 6-7 inches wide. Apply even pressure so the filling spreads without tearing the dough. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Roll for approximately 1 minute until the surface looks evenly flattened.

Heat a tawa until moderately hot and place one rolled paratha on it. Flame level: medium. Cook for 1-2 minutes until small bubbles appear on the upper surface and the underside develops pale brown spots.

Flip the paratha and spread approximately 1 tsp ghee over the cooked side. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 1-2 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the surface develops golden patches and the edges begin to crisp.

Flip once more, apply another little ghee, and cook the second side thoroughly. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 1-2 minutes until both sides are golden brown, crisp in places, and cooked through without raw dough in the centre.

Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining portions. Flame level: medium-low. Cook each paratha for approximately 4-5 minutes, adjusting the heat if the surface browns too quickly. Serve hot with curd, pickle, or butter.
tips: Keep the potato filling relatively dry and mash it thoroughly to prevent the parathas from tearing.
Do not roll too aggressively after stuffing; gentle, even pressure helps distribute the filling.

title: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
description: Tangy yoghurt and gram flour kadhi simmered slowly with onion pakoras and finished with a fragrant cumin and dried chilli tempering.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.amount: 2 tbsp for kadhi and enough for frying pakoras

steps: Whisk the curd with 1/2 cup kadhi besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt until completely smooth. Gradually add 4 cups water while whisking to prevent lumps. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 3 minutes until the liquid is uniform and pourable.
Heat oil in a kadai and add the sliced onions, chopped green chilli, ajwain, and a pinch of salt. Flame level: medium. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until the onions soften and release their sharp raw aroma.

Add the remaining pakora besan and enough water to bind the onions into a thick, spoonable mixture. Mix until the batter coats the onion strands without becoming runny. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 2 minutes mixing until no dry flour remains.

Heat oil in a separate deep kadai for frying. Drop small portions of the onion mixture carefully into the hot oil. Flame level: medium. Fry for 5-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pakoras become golden brown, crisp outside, and cooked through. Drain on a plate.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot and add fenugreek seeds and half the cumin seeds. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 30 seconds until the cumin crackles and the fenugreek releases a slightly nutty aroma without turning dark.

Pour the prepared yoghurt-besan mixture into the pot while stirring continuously. Bring it to a gentle boil, stirring frequently so the besan does not settle at the bottom. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for 5-6 minutes until bubbles appear across the surface and the raw besan smell begins to disappear.

Reduce the heat and simmer the kadhi, stirring every few minutes to prevent sticking. Flame level: low. Cook for 20-25 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly, turns creamy, and loses its raw yoghurt-besan taste. Add a little water if it becomes too thick.

Add the fried pakoras and simmer until they soften slightly and absorb the kadhi. Flame level: low. Cook for 4-5 minutes. Separately heat 1 tsp oil, add the remaining cumin, dried red chillies, and hing, and cook over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour the tempering over the kadhi and garnish with coriander.
tips: Slightly sour curd gives kadhi its characteristic tangy flavour.
Keep stirring during the initial boiling stage to prevent the besan from forming lumps or sticking to the bottom.

title: Paneer Bhurji
description: Crumbled paneer cooked with onions, tomatoes, green chillies, and everyday spices into a quick, flavourful dry-style Indian scramble.
steps: Crumble the paneer with clean fingers or a fork into small, irregular pieces. Keep some slightly larger pieces for texture rather than making a fine paste. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 2 minutes preparing the paneer until it resembles coarse scrambled eggs.
Heat oil and butter together in a kadai. Add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle until fragrant. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds, taking care that the butter does not turn dark.

Add chopped onions and green chillies. Sauté, stirring frequently, until the onions soften and become translucent with lightly golden edges. Flame level: medium. Cook for 4-5 minutes until the raw onion smell disappears.
Add ginger and garlic. Stir continuously so the garlic cooks evenly without burning. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the sharp raw aroma fades and the mixture smells savoury.

Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook while stirring and pressing the tomatoes gently until they soften into a thick masala. Flame level: medium. Cook for 4-5 minutes until moisture reduces and oil begins to appear around the edges.

Add the crumbled paneer and fold it gently into the masala. Avoid pressing it too firmly, which can make the mixture dense. Flame level: low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the paneer is heated through and evenly coated.

Sprinkle garam masala and half the chopped coriander over the bhurji. Stir gently until the spices release their aroma and the mixture looks moist rather than watery. Flame level: low. Cook for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice, and garnish with the remaining coriander. Rest for 2 minutes until the flavours settle. Serve hot with roti, paratha, or toasted bread.
tips: Use fresh, soft paneer for a moist bhurji.
Do not cook the paneer for too long after adding it, or it may become rubbery.

title: Kanda Poha
description: A light Maharashtrian breakfast made with flattened rice, onions, peanuts, curry leaves, turmeric, and a fresh squeeze of lemon.
steps: Place the poha in a sieve and rinse gently under running water for approximately 20-30 seconds. Drain thoroughly and leave undisturbed until the flakes soften but remain separate. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for 5 minutes until the poha feels soft when pressed but does not turn mushy.

Heat the oil in a wide kadai and add the peanuts. Stir frequently so they roast evenly. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the peanuts become crisp and develop a roasted aroma. Remove and keep aside.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds to the remaining oil. Flame level: medium. Cook for 20-30 seconds until the mustard seeds pop and the cumin becomes fragrant.

Add curry leaves and chopped green chillies carefully, followed by the chopped onion. Flame level: medium. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until the onion turns translucent and the curry leaves release their aroma.

Add turmeric, sugar, and salt. Stir briefly to distribute the seasoning through the onions. Flame level: low. Cook for 30 seconds until the turmeric colours the oil evenly and the mixture smells fragrant.

Add the softened poha and roasted peanuts. Fold gently from the sides so the turmeric coats the flakes without crushing them. Flame level: low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the poha is heated through and the colour looks evenly yellow.

Turn off the heat and add lemon juice and chopped coriander. Mix gently until the citrus aroma becomes noticeable and the seasoning is evenly distributed. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for 2 minutes.
Garnish with grated coconut if desired and serve warm. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Allow 1 minute for the poha to settle before serving with tea or a side of curd.
tips: Use thick poha rather than thin poha, which can become mushy after rinsing.
Rinse briefly instead of soaking in a bowl of water.

title: Vegetable Upma
description: A savoury semolina breakfast cooked with vegetables, curry leaves, mustard seeds, and green chillies until soft, fluffy, and aromatic.
steps: Heat a dry kadai and add the semolina. Stir continuously so it roasts evenly without changing colour significantly. Flame level: low. Roast for 4-5 minutes until the grains feel dry, smell lightly nutty, and remain pale. Transfer to a plate.

In the same kadai, heat oil and ghee. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, and cashews. Flame level: medium. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the mustard seeds crackle, the dals turn light golden, and the cashews become lightly toasted.
Add curry leaves, green chillies, and chopped ginger carefully. Stir until the leaves become fragrant and the ginger loses its raw smell. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for approximately 1 minute.
Add the chopped onion, carrot, beans, and green peas. Stir-fry until the onion softens and the vegetables begin to lose their raw, firm appearance. Flame level: medium. Cook for 3-4 minutes.

Pour in the water and add salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil, stirring once or twice so the seasoning dissolves evenly. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for 3-4 minutes until bubbles cover the surface and the vegetables are nearly tender.

Reduce the heat and slowly sprinkle in the roasted semolina while stirring continuously with a whisk or wooden spoon. Flame level: medium-low. Spend 2-3 minutes adding and mixing until the grains absorb the water without forming lumps.
Cover the kadai and allow the semolina to steam until fully cooked. Flame level: low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the upma becomes fluffy, the water is absorbed, and no raw semolina taste remains.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice, and fluff gently with a spoon. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for 2 minutes until the texture settles, then serve warm.
tips: Roasting the semolina before cooking helps produce a fluffy texture and prevents a raw flour taste.
Add the semolina gradually while stirring to avoid lumps.

title: South Indian Sambar
description: A comforting lentil and vegetable stew simmered with tamarind, sambar powder, and a fragrant mustard seed and curry leaf tempering.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 3 cups for dal, plus 3 cups for sambar

ingredients.name: tamarind
ingredients.amount: 1 tbsp, soaked in 1/2 cup warm water

steps: Rinse the toor dal until the water runs mostly clear and transfer it to a pressure cooker with 3 cups water and turmeric. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for approximately 15-18 minutes after pressure builds, until the dal becomes completely soft. Allow pressure to release naturally.

Mash the cooked dal with a ladle until smooth and creamy. Add a little warm water if it is too thick. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend 2 minutes mashing until no large lumps remain.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot and add the peeled small onions. Sauté until they develop light golden spots and smell sweet rather than sharp. Flame level: medium. Cook for 3-4 minutes.

Add the carrot, drumsticks, and chopped tomato. Stir briefly, then add 2 cups water and half the salt. Flame level: medium-high. Bring to a boil and cook for 5-7 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften but still hold their shape.

Extract the tamarind pulp by squeezing the soaked tamarind through a sieve. Add the pulp, sambar powder, and remaining salt to the vegetables. Flame level: medium. Simmer for 5 minutes until the tamarind aroma mellows and the vegetables become nearly tender.

Add the mashed dal and remaining water, stirring until the mixture becomes uniform. Flame level: low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sambar thickens slightly, small bubbles appear, and the raw smell of the sambar powder disappears.

Heat the remaining oil in a small tempering pan. Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30-45 seconds until the mustard seeds crackle and the curry leaves release their aroma.
Pour the tempering into the simmering sambar and stir gently. Flame level: low. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the aromas combine, then turn off the heat and garnish with fresh coriander.
tips: Add tamarind after the vegetables have started softening so they cook properly.
Adjust the final water quantity according to whether you prefer thick sambar for idli or a thinner version for rice.

title: Lemon Rice
description: A bright, tangy South Indian rice preparation tempered with mustard seeds, peanuts, curry leaves, turmeric, and fresh lemon juice.
steps: Spread the cooked rice on a wide plate and separate any clumps gently with a fork. Allow it to cool until the grains feel firm and separate. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for approximately 5 minutes if the rice is freshly cooked.

Heat oil in a wide kadai and add the peanuts. Stir regularly so they roast evenly without burning. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the peanuts become crisp and smell toasted. Remove and set aside.
Add mustard seeds, urad dal, and chana dal to the same oil. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30-45 seconds until the mustard seeds pop and the dals become light golden.

Add dried red chillies, green chilli, curry leaves, and hing carefully. Stir until the curry leaves crackle and the dried chillies release their aroma. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for approximately 1 minute.
Add turmeric powder and salt, stirring quickly so the turmeric colours the oil evenly. Flame level: low. Cook for 20-30 seconds until the raw turmeric smell fades without allowing it to burn.

Add the separated rice and roasted peanuts. Toss gently with a spatula, lifting from the bottom so the grains remain intact. Flame level: low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the rice is evenly yellow and heated through.

Turn off the heat and pour in the lemon juice. Mix gently until the citrus aroma spreads through the rice and the seasoning tastes balanced. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 1 minute mixing.
Garnish with chopped coriander and rest for 2 minutes before serving. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Serve warm or at room temperature with papad or curd.
tips: Use cooled, separate rice so the final dish does not become sticky.
Add lemon juice after switching off the heat to preserve its fresh, tangy flavour.

title: Lauki Kofta Curry
description: Soft bottle gourd dumplings made with gram flour, fried until golden, and served in a gently spiced onion-tomato gravy.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.amount: 2 tbsp for gravy and enough for frying

steps: Grate the peeled bottle gourd and squeeze out most of its liquid into a separate bowl. Keep the squeezed liquid aside for the gravy if desired. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 3 minutes until the grated lauki feels moist but does not release water when lightly pressed.

Combine the grated lauki with besan, chopped green chilli, ginger, red chilli powder, cumin powder, and half the salt. Mix until the ingredients form a thick mixture that can hold its shape. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 2-3 minutes, adding a little more besan only if the mixture feels too loose.

Heat oil in a deep kadai for frying. Shape the lauki mixture into small round koftas and carefully slide them into the oil in batches. Flame level: medium. Fry for 5-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until the koftas are evenly golden brown and firm outside. Drain on a plate.
Heat 2 tbsp fresh oil in another kadai and add cumin seeds. Flame level: medium. Cook for 20-30 seconds until they crackle and release a warm, nutty aroma.

Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown, stirring frequently to prevent uneven browning. Flame level: medium. Cook for 5-6 minutes until the onions soften and their raw smell disappears. Add garlic and cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.

Add tomato puree, turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and remaining salt. Stir well and cook until the gravy thickens and oil begins separating around the edges. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 6-8 minutes until the raw tomato aroma disappears.

Add 1.5 cups water or reserved lauki liquid and bring the gravy to a gentle simmer. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for 3-4 minutes until bubbles appear and the gravy reaches a smooth, pourable consistency.

Add the fried koftas and garam masala just before serving. Spoon gravy over them gently so they absorb flavour without breaking apart. Flame level: low. Simmer for 3-4 minutes until the koftas soften slightly, then garnish with coriander and serve.
tips: Squeeze excess moisture from the grated lauki before mixing the kofta batter.
Add koftas shortly before serving so they do not become excessively soft in the gravy.

title: Methi Thepla
description: Soft Gujarati flatbreads made with fresh fenugreek leaves, whole wheat flour, yoghurt, and mild spices, cooked on a tawa until lightly golden.

ingredients.name: oil
ingredients.amount: 2 tbsp for dough, plus extra for cooking

steps: Pick the fresh fenugreek leaves, discard thick stems, and wash thoroughly. Drain and chop finely. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes preparing the leaves until no visible dirt or excess water remains.

Combine whole wheat flour, besan, chopped methi, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, sesame seeds, sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 2 minutes until the fenugreek is evenly distributed through the flour.

Add curd, grated ginger, green chilli, and 2 tbsp oil. Mix and knead, adding water gradually only if required, until a soft, smooth dough forms. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Knead for 4-5 minutes until the dough feels supple and does not stick excessively to the fingers.
Cover the dough and allow it to rest. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for 10 minutes until the flour hydrates and the dough becomes easier to roll.

Divide the dough into 10-12 equal balls. Dust each with flour and roll into a thin circle approximately 6 inches wide. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Roll each portion for approximately 1 minute until the surface is even and the edges are not cracked.
Heat a tawa and place one rolled thepla on it. Flame level: medium. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear and pale spots form underneath, then flip carefully.

Spread a little oil over the upper surface and flip again. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 1-2 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until golden-brown spots appear and the thepla puffs slightly in places.

Apply a little oil to the other side and cook until both sides are evenly cooked and the surface feels soft with lightly crisp edges. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for another 1 minute, then transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining dough.
tips: Dry the fenugreek leaves well after washing so the dough does not become unexpectedly sticky.
Theplas should remain soft and flexible rather than being cooked as crisp as papad.

title: Maharashtrian Misal Pav
description: A spicy Maharashtrian curry made with sprouted moth beans, topped with crunchy farsan, chopped onions, coriander, and lemon, served with toasted pav.
steps: Rinse the sprouted moth beans thoroughly and transfer them to a pressure cooker with 2 cups water and a little salt. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for approximately 10-12 minutes after pressure builds, until the sprouts are tender but retain their shape.
Heat oil in a kadai and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until the seeds crackle and the curry leaves release their aroma.
Add chopped onions and sauté, stirring regularly, until they become golden and slightly caramelised. Flame level: medium. Cook for 5-6 minutes until the sharp raw onion smell disappears.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant. Flame level: medium-low. Stir for 1-2 minutes until the raw smell fades without allowing the garlic to brown too much.

Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, misal masala, and salt. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 6-8 minutes until the tomatoes become soft, the masala thickens, and oil begins appearing around the edges.
Add the cooked moth beans with their cooking liquid and approximately 1 cup additional water. Flame level: medium-high. Bring to a boil for 3-4 minutes until bubbles appear throughout the curry.

Reduce the heat and simmer until the usal develops a moderately thick consistency. Flame level: low. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans absorb the masala and the gravy smells deeply spiced.

Place the usal in serving bowls and top with farsan, chopped onion, coriander, and lemon juice. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Toast the pav with a little butter over medium-low flame for 1-2 minutes until lightly golden, then serve immediately.
tips: Add farsan immediately before serving so it remains crunchy.
Adjust the misal masala according to its spice level and salt content.

title: Gujarati Dal Dhokli
description: A comforting Gujarati one-pot meal featuring wheat flour pieces simmered in mildly sweet, tangy, and spiced toor dal.
steps: Rinse the toor dal thoroughly and transfer it to a pressure cooker with 2 cups water and turmeric. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for approximately 12-15 minutes after pressure builds until the lentils become completely soft.

Mash the cooked dal until smooth and transfer it to a large pot with 3 cups water, chopped tomato, peanuts, jaggery, tamarind pulp, chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Flame level: medium. Bring to a gentle boil for 4-5 minutes until the jaggery dissolves.

Combine wheat flour, a little turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and 1 tsp oil in a bowl. Add water gradually and knead into a firm, smooth dough. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Knead for 4-5 minutes until no dry flour remains.

Divide the dough into portions and roll each into a thin circle approximately 2 mm thick. Cut into small diamond or square pieces. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes until all the dhokli pieces are evenly sized.

Bring the dal mixture to a steady simmer and gradually add the dhokli pieces one at a time, stirring gently to prevent sticking. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the mixture returns to a boil.

Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally so the dhokli does not settle at the bottom. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 12-15 minutes until the wheat pieces become soft and cooked through and the dal thickens.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and hing. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until the seeds crackle and the leaves become fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the dal dhokli and mix gently. Flame level: low. Simmer for another 1-2 minutes until the aromas combine, then garnish with coriander and serve hot.
tips: Keep the dough firm so the dhokli pieces retain their shape while simmering.
Add warm water if the dal becomes too thick during cooking.

title: Rava Idli
description: Soft, steamed South Indian semolina cakes prepared with yoghurt, vegetables, cashews, and a fragrant tempering.
steps: Heat a dry kadai and add semolina. Stir continuously to roast it evenly without browning. Flame level: low. Roast for 4-5 minutes until the rava smells lightly nutty and feels dry, then transfer to a bowl to cool.
Heat oil in the same kadai and add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, and cashews. Flame level: medium. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the mustard seeds crackle and the dals turn light golden.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and grated ginger. Flame level: medium-low. Sauté for approximately 1 minute until the leaves become fragrant and the raw ginger smell fades.
Add the grated carrot and cook briefly until it softens slightly. Flame level: medium. Stir for 2 minutes until the carrot loses its raw smell but retains some texture.

Combine the roasted rava, prepared tempering, curd, salt, and approximately 1/2 cup water. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 2 minutes until a thick, pourable batter forms, then rest for 10 minutes to allow the semolina to absorb moisture.
Prepare a steamer with water and grease the idli moulds. Bring the water to a steady boil. Flame level: high. Heat for approximately 5 minutes until visible steam rises consistently.

Add eno fruit salt to the rested batter and mix gently for 10-15 seconds until it becomes slightly airy. Spoon immediately into the greased moulds and place them in the steamer. Flame level: medium-high. Steam for 12-15 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Switch off the heat and rest the idlis for 3 minutes before removing them carefully with a spoon. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Serve warm with coconut chutney or sambar.
tips: Do not overmix after adding eno because the batter can lose its aeration.
Allow the idlis to rest briefly before removing them to prevent sticking.

title: Khaman Dhokla
description: Soft and spongy Gujarati gram flour cakes steamed until fluffy and finished with a sweet, tangy mustard seed tempering.
steps: Sift besan into a mixing bowl to remove lumps. Add turmeric, salt, sugar, lemon juice, and approximately 3/4 cup water gradually. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Whisk for 3 minutes until the batter becomes smooth, thick, and pourable.
Prepare a steamer with sufficient water and grease a round or square metal tin with oil. Bring the water to a boil. Flame level: high. Heat for approximately 5 minutes until steady steam develops.
Add eno fruit salt to the batter and pour 1 tbsp water over it. Mix gently in one direction for 10-15 seconds until the batter becomes airy and slightly foamy.

Immediately pour the batter into the greased tin and place it inside the steamer. Flame level: medium-high. Steam for 15-18 minutes until the dhokla rises, feels springy, and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

Switch off the steamer and leave the dhokla inside for 3 minutes before removing the tin. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Allow it to cool for approximately 5 minutes until firm enough to cut cleanly.

Heat oil in a small pan and add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, green chillies, and curry leaves. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30-40 seconds until the mustard seeds crackle and the sesame seeds turn lightly golden.
Add 1/3 cup water and 2 tsp sugar to the tempering. Flame level: medium-low. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the liquid becomes lightly syrupy.

Cut the dhokla into squares and pour the tempering evenly over the pieces. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, then garnish with coriander and serve.
tips: Steam the batter immediately after adding eno to retain its airiness.
Pour the tempering gradually so the dhokla absorbs moisture evenly without becoming soggy.

title: Gujarati Vegetable Handvo
description: A savoury Gujarati savoury cake made with fermented rice and lentil batter, grated vegetables, sesame seeds, and a crisp tempered crust.
steps: Wash the rice and all three dals thoroughly and soak them together in plenty of water. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Soak for 4-5 hours until the grains soften and become easier to grind.

Drain the soaked mixture and grind it with curd and a little water into a coarse, thick batter. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Grind for 2-3 minutes until no large whole grains remain, then transfer to a bowl.

Cover the batter and allow it to ferment in a warm place. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for approximately 6-8 hours until it becomes slightly airy and develops a mild tangy aroma.

Add grated bottle gourd, carrot, ginger, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, sugar, and salt. Mix until the vegetables are evenly distributed and the batter remains thick. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Mix for 2 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy, deep pan and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until the seeds crackle and smell toasted.

Add eno to the batter and fold gently. Pour the batter over the tempering and spread it evenly in the pan. Flame level: low. Cover and cook for 12-15 minutes until the base becomes golden and the centre begins to set.

Carefully flip the handvo using a plate or wide spatula, adding a little oil around the edges. Flame level: low to medium-low. Cook uncovered for another 10-12 minutes until the second side becomes crisp and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Remove the handvo and allow it to rest for 5 minutes before cutting into wedges. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Serve warm with green chutney or plain curd.
tips: The batter should be thick rather than runny so the handvo holds its shape.
Use a heavy pan and moderate heat to cook the centre without burning the crust.

title: Kerala Kadala Curry
description: A traditional Kerala black chickpea curry with roasted coconut, curry leaves, and warming spices, commonly served with puttu or appam.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 4 cups for pressure cooking, plus extra as needed

steps: Wash the black chickpeas and soak them in plenty of water for 8-12 hours. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest until the chickpeas become visibly plumper, then drain and rinse thoroughly.

Transfer the chickpeas to a pressure cooker with 4 cups fresh water and half the salt. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for approximately 25-30 minutes after pressure builds until the chickpeas become completely tender.
Heat a dry kadai and add grated coconut and fennel seeds. Flame level: low. Roast for 5-7 minutes, stirring continuously, until the coconut turns golden brown and develops a toasted aroma.

Add coriander powder, chilli powder, and turmeric to the roasted coconut. Flame level: low. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, then allow the mixture to cool and grind with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a kadai and add mustard seeds, cinnamon, and curry leaves. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until the mustard seeds pop and the leaves release their aroma.
Add sliced onion, ginger, garlic, and green chilli. Flame level: medium. Sauté for 5-6 minutes until the onion becomes soft and golden at the edges and the garlic smells cooked.
Add chopped tomato and cook until it softens into the onion mixture. Flame level: medium-low. Stir for 4-5 minutes until the tomato loses its raw smell and begins forming a thick masala.

Add the ground coconut paste, cooked chickpeas, remaining salt, and approximately 1 cup cooking liquid. Flame level: low. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until the gravy thickens, coats the chickpeas, and develops a rich roasted-coconut aroma.
tips: Roast the coconut slowly because it can turn bitter if it burns.
Mash a few chickpeas into the gravy if you prefer a thicker consistency.

title: Rajasthani Gatte Ki Sabzi
description: A traditional Rajasthani curry featuring gram flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yoghurt-based gravy with cumin and aromatic spices.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.amount: 4 cups for boiling gatte, plus 1 cup for gravy

steps: Combine besan, ajwain, half the chilli powder, a little turmeric, salt, and 1 tbsp oil in a bowl. Add water gradually and knead into a firm dough. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Knead for 3-4 minutes until smooth and non-sticky.

Divide the dough into portions and roll each into a long cylinder approximately 1 inch thick. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend 3 minutes shaping the cylinders evenly so they cook at the same rate.

Bring 4 cups water to a boil in a large pot and carefully add the besan cylinders. Flame level: high. Boil for 12-15 minutes until the cylinders become firm and a knife inserted into the centre comes out clean.

Remove the cylinders and allow them to cool slightly. Reserve 1 cup of the cooking water and cut the cylinders into 1-inch pieces. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Rest for approximately 5 minutes until easy to handle.
Heat the remaining oil in a kadai and add cumin seeds and hing. Flame level: medium. Cook for 20-30 seconds until the cumin crackles and releases its aroma.
Add ginger and green chilli, followed by coriander powder and the remaining turmeric and chilli powder. Flame level: low. Stir for 30-45 seconds until fragrant without allowing the spices to burn.

Reduce the flame and gradually add whisked curd while stirring continuously. Flame level: low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes smooth and warm without splitting. Add the reserved cooking water and bring to a gentle simmer.

Add the gatte pieces and salt, then simmer gently until the dumplings absorb the gravy. Flame level: low. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the curry thickens and the besan pieces become flavourful. Finish with garam masala and coriander.
tips: Keep the dough firm so the gatte do not disintegrate while boiling.
Add yoghurt over low heat and stir continuously to reduce the chance of curdling.

title: Tomato Sev Sabzi
description: A quick Rajasthani curry made with tangy tomatoes, everyday spices, and crunchy gram flour sev added just before serving.
steps: Wash and finely chop the tomatoes, onion, ginger, and green chilli. Keep the sev separate until the final stage. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes preparing the ingredients.
Heat oil in a kadai and add cumin seeds and mustard seeds. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until the mustard seeds crackle and the cumin releases a toasted aroma.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent with lightly golden edges. Flame level: medium. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring regularly so the onion does not burn.
Add ginger and green chilli and sauté briefly. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant and the sharp raw smell disappears.

Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, sugar, and salt. Flame level: medium. Cook for 6-8 minutes until the tomatoes collapse into a thick, glossy masala and oil begins separating.
Add approximately 1 cup water and stir to create a smooth gravy. Flame level: medium-high. Bring to a boil for 2-3 minutes until bubbles appear throughout and the consistency becomes pourable.

Reduce the heat and simmer the gravy briefly, adjusting salt and water if necessary. Flame level: low. Cook for 3 minutes until the spices combine and the tomato flavour becomes rounded rather than sharply raw.
Add the sev just before serving and fold gently into the gravy. Flame level: low. Cook for 30-60 seconds until some sev softens while the rest retains texture. Finish with garam masala and coriander.
tips: Use thick sev if you want it to retain some texture in the gravy.
Do not add sev too early because it absorbs liquid and can become excessively soft.

title: Maharashtrian Bharli Vangi
description: Small brinjals stuffed with a roasted peanut, sesame, coconut, and spice mixture, then simmered in a thick Maharashtrian-style gravy.
steps: Wash the small brinjals and remove their stems while keeping the tops intact. Make two intersecting slits from the bottom without cutting completely through. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes preparing them and keep submerged in water to prevent discolouration.

Heat a dry kadai and add peanuts. Roast until lightly browned, then add sesame seeds and grated coconut. Flame level: low. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring continuously, until the mixture smells nutty and the coconut turns lightly golden.

Allow the roasted mixture to cool, then grind it with god masala, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, jaggery, tamarind pulp, and salt. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Grind for 1-2 minutes until a coarse, thick stuffing forms.

Drain the brinjals and carefully fill each slit with the prepared stuffing. Reserve any extra stuffing for the gravy. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend approximately 5 minutes until the brinjals are evenly filled without breaking.
Heat oil in a wide kadai and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Flame level: medium. Cook for 30 seconds until they crackle and release their aroma.

Add chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste. Flame level: medium. Sauté for 4-5 minutes until the onion becomes golden and the raw garlic smell disappears. Add chopped tomato and reserved stuffing, cooking for another 3-4 minutes until the masala thickens.

Arrange the stuffed brinjals in the kadai and turn them gently to coat with the masala. Add approximately 1 cup water, cover, and cook. Flame level: low. Cook for 15-18 minutes, turning carefully once or twice, until the brinjals become completely tender.

Uncover and simmer briefly to thicken the gravy. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 3-4 minutes until oil appears around the edges and the stuffing has blended into the sauce. Garnish with coriander and serve hot.
tips: Choose small, tender brinjals of similar size so they cook evenly.
Handle the stuffed brinjals gently because they become delicate as they soften.

title: Pav Bhaji
description: A popular Mumbai street-style dish of mashed vegetables cooked with butter, tomatoes, and pav bhaji masala, served with toasted bread rolls.
steps: Wash and chop the potatoes, cauliflower, carrot, and capsicum into small pieces. Transfer the potatoes, cauliflower, carrot, and peas to a pressure cooker with 1.5 cups water and a little salt. Flame level: medium-high. Cook for approximately 8-10 minutes after pressure builds until the vegetables become soft.

Release the pressure safely and transfer the cooked vegetables to a large bowl. Mash thoroughly until mostly smooth, leaving a few small pieces for texture. Flame level: low, with the stove switched off. Spend 2-3 minutes mashing until no large hard pieces remain.
Heat oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide kadai. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden. Flame level: medium. Cook for 4-5 minutes until the raw onion smell disappears.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chopped capsicum. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and the capsicum begins to soften while retaining some bite.

Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, and salt. Flame level: medium. Cook for 6-8 minutes, mashing the tomatoes with the back of a spoon until the mixture becomes thick and glossy.

Add the mashed vegetables and approximately 1/2 cup water. Mix thoroughly, then mash everything together using a potato masher. Flame level: medium-low. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the bhaji becomes uniform, thick, and aromatic.
Add the remaining butter and lemon juice, then mix until the butter melts into the bhaji. Flame level: low. Simmer for another 2 minutes until the surface looks glossy and the flavours are balanced.

Slice the pav horizontally and heat a tawa with a little butter. Flame level: medium-low. Toast the pav for 1-2 minutes on each side until lightly crisp and golden. Garnish the bhaji with coriander and serve with chopped onion and lemon wedges.
tips: Mash the vegetables thoroughly for the characteristic smooth pav bhaji texture.
Add butter near the end for a richer finish without making the masala greasy.
